Türkiye Mining & Quarrying Accidents — a public record

This is a record of people who went to work in Türkiye's mines and quarries and did not come home. Every value traces to cited source documents through recorded reviewer decisions. It exists for remembrance and accountability — not comparison, not spectacle.

Records are seeded from open tertiary sources (Wikidata, Wikipedia) and await corroboration against official and professional-chamber sources. Coverage is partial: years without a mark are years without a published, reviewed record — not years without loss.

Where it happened — and where mining happens

Marker area reflects the number of people who died. Solid markers are facility-approximate locations — the mine or its vicinity, never an exact point. Hollow dashed circles summarize records without published coordinates at their province's reference point. Gray diamonds are documented mining sites from open structured sources — a fraction of licensed operations, shown for context. Select any marker to read more.

accident record (area = people lost) documented mining site (partial coverage)

People lost, year by year

Blue bars: people who died in this register's published incident records. Gray line: İSİG Meclisi's sector-wide annual miner work-death totals (all causes) — a broader measure, not comparable to the bars. The pale gray columns between them are deaths that were counted but never became a publicly recorded incident. Dashed vertical lines mark public-record events (descriptive only — this chart makes no causal claim). Hover a year for the figures. The chart always shows the full register; filters above apply to the map and the tables.

How dangerous, compared to elsewhere

Coal-mining deaths per 100 million tonnes produced — the one rate this project shows, because its exposure denominator is documented. Figures as cited by press sources referenced in the retrieved source text; methodologies differ across countries, so this is an indicative comparison (an official TÜİK/TKİ-based series is an open task).

What the sources say happened

Reported event mechanisms — never a root cause and never a statement of legal responsibility (see the cause coding protocol). Counted over published records with a source-backed classification.

Documented mining sites

Mining and quarrying sites documented in open structured sources (Wikidata, CC0), registered through the same evidence pipeline as the accident records: every row keeps its source link. Coverage is partial — these are the sites open data documents, a fraction of the operations licensed in Türkiye; absence from this table means nothing. Operator and ownership entries appear only where the source states them, with their assertion status; operating status is shown only when the source asserts it. Fuller registers (Global Energy Monitor, MAPEG licence data) are open assessment tasks.

If nothing changes
